fullPassage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.

❌ ③ unseen: unseen(보이지 않는)은 invisible과 유사
❌ ④ obscure: obscure(잘 보이지 않는)는 invisible과 유사
det.tip: feeling invisible(무시당하는 느낌) ↔ noticed(주목받는)

questions.passage:
(A) After the long hike through the dark forest, she had a strong <u>sense</u> that something was quietly watching her.
(B) A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic <u>sense</u> of the word.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 sense의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 느낌/감각 — (B) 의미/뜻: (A)는 무언가가 지켜본다는 '느낌', (B)는 'in the most classic sense of the word'로 단어의 '의미/뜻'을 나타내어 다의어의 두 의미를 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ② (A) 의미 — (B) 느낌: (A)는 느낌이 적절
❌ ③ (A) 느낌/감각 — (B) 분별력: (B)의 sense는 분별력이 아닌 의미
❌ ④ (A) 방향 — (B) 의미/뜻: (A)는 방향이 아닌 느낌
det.tip: sense: ① (명사) 느낌/감각 ② (명사) 의미/뜻 ③ (명사) 분별력 ④ (동사) 감지하다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a careful plan or method designed to achieve a particular goal"

det.korean: strategy=전략 (특정 목표를 이루기 위한 신중한 계획/방법)
det.analysis:
❌ ① anger: anger(화)는 계획/방법이 아닌 감정
✅ ② strategy: strategy(전략)는 특정 목표를 이루기 위한 신중한 계획/방법으로 영영 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ punishment: punishment(처벌)는 목표 달성 계획이 아님
❌ ④ neuropsychologist: neuropsychologist(신경심리학자)는 사람을 가리킴
det.tip: strategy = 전략. adopting a different strategy가 본문 단서

questions.passage: Instead of __________ (discourage) the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.analysis: 'Instead of __________'에서 전치사 of 뒤에는 명사 역할을 하는 동명사(V-ing)가 와야 한다. instead of + V-ing = ~하는 대신에. discourage → discouraging
det.tip: instead of + V-ing(동명사): instead of discouraging = 막는 대신에

questions.passage: For a child who feels lonely, __________ (be) scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.analysis: 문장의 주어 자리이고 '꾸중을 듣는 것'이라는 수동의 의미이므로 동명사 being + 과거분사 scolded(= being scolded, 꾸중을 듣는 것)가 적절. be → being. is much better의 주어 역할을 하는 동명사구
det.tip: being + 과거분사 = 동명사 수동태 (being scolded = 꾸중을 듣는 것)

questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than feeling invisible, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly __________, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: pointing out the negatives=부정적인 것을 지적하는 것 — 이를 계속하는 대신 긍정적인 것을 보상
det.analysis:
❌ ① rewarding good behavior(좋은 행동을 보상): 이것은 뒤의 reward the positives와 같아 '~대신'의 대조가 성립 안 함
❌ ② ignoring the child completely(아이를 완전히 무시): 본문과 무관
❌ ③ praising every small success(작은 성공마다 칭찬): 긍정적 행위로 대조 불성립
✅ ④ pointing out the negatives(부정적인 것을 지적): 원문 일치. '부정적인 것을 계속 지적하는 대신' 긍정적인 것을 보상한다는 대조에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives

questions.passage: Punishing a child may not be effective due to what Álvaro Bilbao, a neuropsychologist, calls 'trick-punishments.' A trick-punishment is a scolding, a moment of anger or a punishment in the most classic sense of the word. Instead of discouraging the child from doing something, it encourages them to do it. For example, Hugh learns that when he hits his little brother, his mother scolds him. For a child who feels lonely, being scolded is much better than __________, so he will continue to hit his brother. In this case, his mother would be better adopting a different strategy. For instance, she could congratulate Hugh when he has not hit his brother for a certain length of time. The mother clearly cannot allow the child to hit his little brother, but instead of constantly pointing out the negatives, she can choose to reward the positives. In this way, any parent can avoid trick-punishments.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: feeling invisible=무시당하는(보이지 않는) 느낌 — 외로운 아이는 이보다 꾸중을 선호
det.analysis:
❌ ① being openly praised(공개적으로 칭찬받는 것): 꾸중보다 못한 상태여야 하므로 부적절
❌ ② getting a special reward(특별한 보상을 받는 것): 꾸중보다 나쁜 상태가 아님
✅ ③ feeling invisible(무시당하는 느낌): 원문 일치. 외로운 아이에게는 '무시당하는 느낌'보다 꾸중이 낫기 때문에 계속 때린다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ playing alone outside(밖에서 혼자 노는 것): 본문과 무관
det.tip: being scolded is much better than feeling invisible — 무시당하는 것보다 꾸중이 낫다
